 Order
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (hybrid/physical) mode.

2. This is the second journey of the petitioner, who having been implicated in connection with Kujanga P.S. Case No.217(2) of 2013 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No.19 of 2016 registered for alleged commission of offence under sections 392, 376 (D)/506/34 of the IPC read with section 6 of the POCSO Act and section 30 of the Arms Act pending on the file of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jagatsinghpur has filed this petition under section 438 of Cr.P.C. for his release on bail in the event of his arrest in the said case.

3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that on the earlier occasion the Petitioner having moved this Court in // 2 // ABLAPL No.18598 of 2019, this Court by order dated 07.01.2020 had directed that in the event the Petitioner surrenders before the learned J.M.F.C.(P), Kujanga within six weeks' and makes a motion of bail, the learned J.M.F.C. (P) shall consider and dispose of the same in accordance with law during the first hour and in case of rejection of the bail application, the Petitioner may move for bail before the next higher forum in the second hour and in that event, the bail application of the Petitioner shall be considered and disposed of by the higher forum in accordance with law on the same day, if there is no other legal impediment.
He submits that since thereafter offence under the provisions of POCSO Act came to be added, the Petitioner could not avail the benefit of the earlier order.

He, therefore, submits that since the Petitioner as yet has not been arrested and the co-accused persons have already been released on bail, since arrest and likely Jagannath @ Jagabandhu Malla vs State Of Odisha ....

detention of the petitioner at this stage would serve no useful purpose, he be granted anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposes the move in view of the nature of offences in which the Petitioner has been implicated.

5. Considering the submissions and on going through the materials available on record as also other surrounding circumstances, while being not inclined to reconsider the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, this application stands disposed of with the observation that in the event the Petitioner surrenders before the court in seisin of the aforesaid // 3 // case within a period of two weeks and moves for his release on bail, the same shall be considered on its own merit; further taking into account the factum of release of co-accused person(s) on bail and if similarly situated with the Petitioner on the ground of parity, as per law and disposed of early in accordance with law without being influenced by this order.
6. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per rules.
(D.Dash) Judge Himansu Signed by: HIMANSU SEKHAR DASH Jagannath @ Jagabandhu Malla vs State Of Odisha ....
